chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn Bahr from Abdullah ibn Muskān from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the camels that belong to the camel-herders, or that are in some of the cities, does zakat apply to them as it applies to the grazing [livestock] in the desert? He said, 'Yes.'
In all these hadiths, the primary narrator is Isḥq ibn ʿAmmār; and if the primary narrator in them is one person, they are not objected to against what we have previously presented from the hadiths.

And although the primary narrator in them is one, their wording differs because in the first hadith he said, 'I asked him,' and did not specify who the questioned one was, and it is possible that he was an Imam or not an Imam.
And in the second report he said, 'I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him),' and in the third hadith he said, 'I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).'

The narrator is one person, so sometimes he narrates it as mursal (without specifying the Imam), and sometimes he narrates from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and sometimes he narrates from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him).
And this fluctuation in it indicates that he narrated it while he was not certain of it.
and whatever follows this pattern is not obligatory to act upon.
And if it were safe from all of that, it would be construed as recommended (mustahabb) rather than obligatory (farḍ) and compulsory (ijab).
And that which indicates that zakat is not obligatory in it except after a full year has passed, added to what we have previously presented, is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Does zakat apply to camels kept in cities, and is it obligatory or recommended?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the zakat liability on urban or kept camels, drawing a parallel to desert grazing livestock. The scholar highlights the narrator Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār’s occasional uncertainty regarding which Imam he consulted, suggesting the ruling is likely recommended (*mustaḥabb*) rather than strictly obligatory (*wājib*). Furthermore, it establishes that zakat is only due after a full lunar year (*ḥawl*) has passed, reinforcing the temporal condition for this specific asset class.
